title: Before the Burial
source: Original CosyWorld writing under the repository MIT license, adapted from the Greek Drama Reader repertoire. See ../ATTRIBUTION.md. No translated passage is quoted.
note: The Bard once sang these couplets verbatim from his prompt. They are lore, not prompt text: no rule, prompt or speech check reads this file. A follow-up turns them into readable book items in the world. Each key is the recital verse choice id in ../card-world.json. An after variant replaced the couplet when its earlier deed already had a receipt.

lines: She laid her brother in the earth.
A raven feather marked his rest.
I set the water by her hands.
She kept a loaf of bread for me.
I set his shield beside the tent.
Tecmessa kept it for her child.
I brought his brother’s written plea.
A rival heard it by the ships.
His rival spoke; I broke the ground.
The camp laid down its quarrel.
I gave him earth beside the ships.
The household kept his shield.
I kept the vigil with their plea.
The witnessed rite gave Ajax earth.
I laid his words beside the bread.
She held the rival’s plea with care.
I laid his words beside the bread.
She named the household in the song.
I laid his words beside the bread.
She heard how witnesses brought earth.
